findings.issue: The recursive walk treats every dict '$ref' key as a reference, without distinguishing schema positions from map-key or data positions. Keys of schema-map keywords (properties, $defs, definitions, patternProperties, dependentSchemas) named '$ref' with object values are rejected as 'non-string reference', and '$ref' keys embedded in annotation/data keywords (const, default, enum, examples, $comment-adjacent payloads) are rejected unless they start with '#'. This over-rejection risks breaking 'preserve existing contracts' for any shipped capability schema that uses '$ref' as a property/definition name or embeds a $ref example as data (plausible in a language-matrix corpus of JSON-Schema examples).
findings.recommendation: Restrict the check to actual schema positions: skip the '$ref' test (but still recurse) when the parent key is a schema-map or annotation keyword, or only flag '$ref' when its value's context is unambiguously a schema.

findings.issue: Only '$ref' is guarded. Other reference-resolving keywords pass through: '$dynamicRef' may hold an absolute URI (external resolution not rejected at load), and an absolute-URI '$id' re-bases fragment-only '$ref's onto an external base — under legacy jsonschema RefResolver semantics a root '$id' of https://... plus '$ref':'#/...' can trigger remote resolution, whereas modern referencing-registry jsonschema resolves it in-document. '$recursiveRef' would be relevant if any 2019-09 schemas are loaded through this same loader (validator is Draft202012, so this is secondary). The offline guarantee therefore depends partly on the jsonschema version/registry behavior, which is not established by the evidence.
findings.recommendation: Also reject absolute-URI '$id' and '$dynamicRef' (or explicitly document that offline safety rests on jsonschema's registry having no network source).

findings.issue: validator.assert_not_called() is vacuous: the exercised path calls only c._load_schema, which never constructs a validator regardless of the guard, so the patch cannot observe ordering. The 'rejected before constructing validator' claim is inferred from code structure, not demonstrated end-to-end through the real entrypoint (e.g. _get_validator() with a poisoned schema). There is also no regression test asserting that the existing on-disk schema corpus still loads, so backwards compatibility of the stricter loader is unverified, and no test of the false-positive contexts in finding 1.
findings.recommendation: Drive the negative case through the production getter with Draft202012Validator patched, and add a corpus test loading every shipped schema plus a positive/negative pair for property-named '$ref'.

findings.issue: (a) New ValueError failure mode added to a loader that previously raised only FileNotFoundError/JSONDecodeError; callers with narrow exception handling may not map it to their expected contract. (b) '$ref': '' is rejected although an empty URI-reference resolves locally per RFC 3986 — stricter than 'allow fragments', though it matches the supplied test. (c) The http/https and '/','./','../' branches are subsumed by the final 'not startswith('#')' branch (any non-'#' ref is rejected anyway); they only improve messages, which is harmless but makes the intended rule ('must be a fragment') implicit.
findings.recommendation: Document ValueError as part of the loader contract and state the effective rule ('$ref must start with #') explicitly in a comment; keep '' rejection only if no shipped schema relies on it.

review.summary: The guard correctly implements the core assignment: any '$ref' not starting with '#' (URLs, file/relative paths, empty, non-string) is rejected inside _load_schema, before any Draft202012Validator is built, and local fragments ('#/$defs/...') pass through and validate real instances, with the controller's 141 offline tests green. It is not fully approvable because the traversal conflates schema positions with property/data positions (false-positive rejections that threaten existing contracts), the offline boundary is only closed for '$ref' while '$dynamicRef' and '$id' re-basing remain unguarded (impact bounded by jsonschema version), and the test evidence does not demonstrate load-before-validator ordering end-to-end nor regression over the existing schema corpus. Remaining uncertainty: whether any shipped capability schema actually contains property- or data-level '$ref' keys, and which jsonschema resolution implementation is in use — both were unverifiable without repository/tool access.

controller_triage: Accept schema-position false positives, missing dynamicRef guard and entrypoint ordering QA gaps. Do not reject all absolute $id without proof: current schema IDs can be legitimate; reviewer version-dependent rebasing claim requires isolated reproduction. No code approval.
